results.title: JoyNews Impact Maker Awardee HOL screens 400 women for breast and cervical cancer in Zebilla
results.content: JoyNews Impact Maker Awardee Haven of Love Children’s Foundation (HOL) has screened 400 women for breast and cervical cancer during a two-day free health outreach in Zebilla in the Upper East Region. The exercise, held on October 28 and 29, 2026, at the Church of Pentecost Auditorium, was organised in collaboration with the Bawku West District Health Directorate’s Zebilla Town Clinic as part of activities marking Breast and Cervical Cancer Awareness Month. All 400 participants received both breast and cervical cancer screening, alongside health education and referral support. Clinical findings identified 17 women with breast-related concerns, including palpable lumps, abnormal nipple discharge and significant breast pain, requiring further clinical assessment and diagnostic investigations. results.title: Remarks on Ningo-Prampram military operation were not an attack on GAF – Sam George
results.content: The Member of Parliament for Ningo-Prampram and Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has met the Defence Minister, the Chief of Defence Staff and the three Service Commanders to discuss a military operation in his constituency that triggered public controversy. The incident occurred last Tuesday when soldiers, allegedly led by Lieutenant Albert Goh, entered Ningo-Prampram and seized trucks belonging to residents at a sand-winning site. Some of the affected drivers alleged that they were assaulted and prevented from working. Following the incident, Mr George called for the dismissal of the officer allegedly involved, describing the conduct as “akin to armed robbery”.

results.title: Parliamentary chief whips call for insurance cover for all government vehicles
results.content: Majority Chief Whip Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor has called for all government vehicles, particularly those operated by ministries, Parliament and other public institutions, to be covered by insurance. Speaking on the floor of Parliament on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, he warned that the failure to insure state vehicles exposes the government to avoidable financial liabilities arising from road crashes. He argued that taxpayers ultimately bear the cost of accidents involving uninsured government vehicles, including compensation and judgment debts awarded by the courts. “The state is killing us twice. The first killing occurs on the asphalt through avoidable road crashes. The second occurs in the courtroom, from where taxpayers' money is compelled to pay avoidable judgment debts for accidents that were to be indemnified by insurance,” he said.

results.title: Sew or buy? The Christmas outfit dilemma facing Ghanaians
results.content: With Christmas approaching, the familiar question of what to wear for the festivities is once again taking shape for many Ghanaians: should they buy ready-made clothes or have a seamstress make an outfit to their taste? For some, buying off the rack offers convenience and avoids the uncertainty of waiting for a tailor-made outfit that may not be ready on time. Others, however, prefer custom-made clothes, which allow them to choose their fabrics, styles and designs. But as the Christmas rush builds, seamstresses say the pressure to meet deadlines is not always entirely of their making. Elizabeth Ockran, a seamstress, says some customers contribute to delays by bringing their fabrics too close to the festive season.
